newsitem.title: USA: House passes $4.6 billion water projects bill.
newsitem.headline: House passes $4.6 billion water projects bill.

text.p: The House Thursday passed a $4.6 billion package put together by House and Senate negotiators to fund water and flood control projects such as dredging, dams and levees.
The legislation for four years of projects was a compromise between the $5.1 billion House bill and a $3.6 billion Senate bill.
With Congress hoping to adjourn this weekend or early next week, the Senate was expected to vote soon on the measure, and send it on to President Clinton who was expected to sign it.

The bill would decrease the federal cost share of flood control projects to 65 percent from 75 percent, raising the local share and and requiring that local governments implement flood plain management plans before they become eligible for flood control projects.

The bill also provided for federal and local cost-sharing to dispose of dredged material from navigation projects, giving the federal government more role in what can be a serious environmental problem.
In another measure pushed by the White House, the bill authorises the administration's plan to restore the Everglades and the south Florida ecosystem.
Backers called it the "greenist" water projects bill ever, with a quarter of its spending directed at restoring or improving the environment in areas including the Chesapeake Bay and the Great Lakes.
Several environmental and conservation groups had opposed the bill, but largely dropped their opposition as spending was cut and changes were made during the House-Senate conference.

"That $3.8 billion is much lower than it was a week ago," said Scott Faber of American Rivers conservation group. That is the federal share of the bill's $4.6 total, with the remainder coming from state and local governments.
Faber said two water projects remained in the bill that environmental groups opposed, but he doubted it would be enough to stop Clinton from signing it.

Those measures were waiving the local cost-share of a $119 million flood control project along the Yazoo River in Mississippi, and authorising a $138 million dam on the Russell Fork of the Big Sandy River in Virginia, Faber said.
Dropped from the bill was a controversial plan to release water from Upper Missouri River reservoirs to lengthen the river's navigational season, regardless of the reservoirs' water levels.
